For ord(alpha,beta)<=m, hmatch applies finite-family uniqueness at depth ord(alpha,beta) to G_m and G_ord. The zero families agree exactly with the same raw f; all required shifts are available strictly below that finite depth. No conclusion about derivatives of unavailable orders is used.
F(0,0)=f holds as exact equality of global function representatives because ord(0,0)=0 and G_0(0,0)=f. Agreement between positive-order representatives is only local almost everywhere.

For each finite m, the budget W_m is retained unchanged. G_m(alpha,beta)=F(alpha,beta) locally almost everywhere converts to equality under volume.restrict Omega using measurability from openness, then RegionL2Budget.congr_ae transfers actual MemLp 2 membership and the integral of the squared norm.

Each successor raises the literal total multiindex order by one. Both fields in a desired weak identity are compared to the same witness G_(ord+1); congr_ae_local transfers the genuine weak derivative identity. No differentiability of a representative at every point is inferred.

ProductLocalWeakDirectional contains local L2 membership for both fields plus the compact smooth test identity. Its test_integrable lemma derives integrability of both displayed test products. The relation is not a purely algebraic assertion about default nonintegrable integrals.

The raw-PDE corollary applies the already supplied finite-order regularity theorem for each m on the same fixed rectangularOpenBox a bY bT. The outer open domain, closed-box inclusion, positive inner widths, strict reserves, positive c, smooth coefficient/source, raw local L2 function and exact weak equation remain explicit input assumptions.

There is no common-in-m norm budget, monotonicity of the chosen budgets, factorial growth estimate, pointwise smooth representative, global-outside-domain derivative claim or executable-selection claim. The file itself discloses its use of classical choice.
